why_v_is_not_rotated.symptom: with K and V rotated (upstream's default for a quantized cache), a conversation read back from the disk tier gave slightly different answers from the same conversation kept in memory
trace: STRIX_STATE_HASH: B's recurrent state was bitwise equal to a resident B after its prompt batches of 8192, 16384 and 24576 tokens and parted at the 1325-token batch to 25901: the first whose attention window (padded to 26112) held free cells, which in the run that had evicted A still carried A's rows
a node-by-node hash of that batch: the first node to differ is the layer-3 sparse attention (qsa3), with identical Q, K and V inputs; only its last query row (position 25900) differs, by 1-2 ulp
zeroing the freed cells makes the runs agree; zeroing only the attention cache's V does, only K or only the indexer does not; zeroing only the padding cells [25901, 26112) does

the selection is causal (no index past its query) and the dequantized V holds no value that is not finite: the last row's 4-key block [25900, 25903] carries three padding keys at probability exactly 0, and the matrix cores' P*V sum still moves in the last bit with their V

f16 shows the same 1-2 ulp difference in every attention layer and the next matmul's rounding absorbs it; a rotated V goes through the inverse rotation first, which spreads it over 64 dimensions, and at layer 23 it survives
why_v_is_not_rotated.decision: V unrotated for qwen4exp (llama-kv-cache.cpp), K rotated: the restored conversation agrees with the resident one batch for batch, KLD within the error of the rotated one
why_v_is_not_rotated.open: the dependence on free cells' contents remains for every type and is absorbed today; zeroing cells as they are freed would remove it
